message.content:
Let  
\[
\mathbf u=\mathbf a-2\mathbf b+3\mathbf c,\qquad 
\mathbf v=2\mathbf a+3\mathbf b-4\mathbf c,\qquad
\mathbf w=p\mathbf b+q\mathbf c.
\]
For \(\mathbf u,\mathbf v,\mathbf w\) to be collinear, \(\mathbf w\) must be an affine combination of \(\mathbf u\) and \(\mathbf v\):
\[
\mathbf w=(1-t)\mathbf u+t\mathbf v
\]
for some scalar \(t\).

Expanding,
\[
\mathbf w=(1-t)(\mathbf a-2\mathbf b+3\mathbf c)+t(2\mathbf a+3\mathbf b-4\mathbf c).
\]
So
\[
\mathbf w=(1+t)\mathbf a+(-2+5t)\mathbf b+(3-7t)\mathbf c.
\]
But \(\mathbf w=p\mathbf b+q\mathbf c\), so the coefficient of \(\mathbf a\) must be \(0\):
\[
1+t=0 \implies t=-1.
\]
Then
\[
p=-2+5(-1)=-7,
\]
and
\[
q=3-7(-1)=10.
\]

Thus the ordered pair is  
\[
\boxed{(-7,10)}.
\]

The answer is (-7,10).
